definitions.explanation: A garden tool with prongs used for gathering leaves or loosening soil. Named for its resemblance to a bear's paw ({熊|くま}の{手|て}).
A decorated bamboo rake sold at Tori-no-Ichi festivals as a good-luck charm for business prosperity. The prongs symbolize raking in good fortune and wealth.

examples.japanese: {熊手|くまで}で{落|お}ち{葉|ば}を{集|あつ}める。
examples.english: To gather fallen leaves with a rake.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{手入|てい}れに{熊手|くまで}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: A rake is needed for garden maintenance.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{公園|こうえん}で{熊手|くまで}を{使|つか}って{落|お}ち{葉|ば}を{掃除|そうじ}する{人|ひと}をよく{見|み}かける。
examples.english: In autumn, you often see people cleaning up fallen leaves with rakes in the park.

examples.japanese: {酉|とり}の{市|いち}で{熊手|くまで}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a lucky charm rake at the Tori-no-Ichi festival.

examples.japanese: {商売|しょうばい}{繁盛|はんじょう}を{願|ねが}って{熊手|くまで}を{飾|かざ}る。
examples.english: We display a lucky rake to pray for business prosperity.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{少|すこ}しずつ{大|おお}きな{熊手|くまで}を{買|か}うのが{縁起|えんぎ}がいいとされている。
examples.english: It is considered auspicious to buy a slightly larger lucky rake each year.

notes:
CULTURE:
The ornamental {熊手|くまで} (sense 2) is a signature item of {酉|とり}の{市|いち} (Tori-no-Ichi), a festival held at shrines in November. Lavishly decorated with lucky symbols — treasure ships, coins, {招|まね}き{猫|ねこ} — these rakes symbolize "raking in" good fortune and prosperity. Businesses and shop owners traditionally buy them to ensure a successful coming year. By custom, buyers start small and purchase progressively larger {熊手|くまで} each year.

The word literally means "bear's hand" ({熊|くま} + {手|て}), describing the claw-like shape of the prongs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {熊手|くまで}で{集|あつ}める: to gather with a rake
- {熊手|くまで}を{飾|かざ}る: to display a lucky rake
- {酉|とり}の{市|いち}の{熊手|くまで}: Tori-no-Ichi lucky rake
- {縁起|えんぎ}{熊手|くまで}: auspicious rake
